items.title: Jay Leonhart interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: in my opinion it was Scott Hamilton. He started playing jazz that people could relate to.

ctx.x: Thank you. Was that about the same time? Did that happen because you wanted to stay home more, and the electric bass became something you needed to do?

Well I never made any real courageous decisions about staying home, it was just sort of little teeny decisions. I took up the electric bass when I was twelve, in 1952. I bought a Humbucker, a Gibson Humbucker, because I was, I don’t know, somehow or other I just bought one and my brother and I were doing a little bit of fooling around with it. And it was in my guitar days, it was before I took the upright up. So I played it, and I said yeah, I can play this, and I’m sort of playing it, and then I put it away.…
nonsense. This saxophone player whose name I’ve just blocked out, the last of the boppers — practiced on the Brooklyn Bridge.
